findings.note: The two files that carry every claim under review are absent from the bundle with no elision notice: the production script (human-copy/plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/resolve-project-context.py, declared sha ca3c95f6...) and the shared test driver (tests/resolve-project-context-block-check.py, declared sha ad84ee05...). Only ten fixture JSON/YAML files were included as declared outputs. Every AC-056 assertion -- _iter_warn_nodes' depth-first walk, _warn_diagnostic_detail's format, one warn entry per outcome:"warn" node, exactly one summary severity:"block" entry, the claimed byte-identical diagnostics[] for the other twelve fixtures -- exists in this bundle only as prose in the implementation report and the contract comment. Per the panel's own rule, no credit can be given for a claim whose code and assertions cannot be read.

AC-024 (REQ-005, named in T-004's own tasks.md Requirements as 'determinism baseline: stable sort of every semantic-output array') requires diagnostics[] to be stable-sorted by (id, detail). The AC-056 fix is described as prepending the per-node warn entries BEFORE the summary severity:"block" entry -- a positional insertion rule, not a sort. Every entry shares the id dsl-warn-on-matched-capability, so ordering is decided purely by detail; the summary detail observed in red-ac056-sh.log is 'a predicate evaluation produced an outcome: warn evidence node', which sorts ahead of any per-node detail naming a capability_id/component_id. The described ordering therefore probably violates AC-024 for the multi-node case (dsl-warn-unsorted-affected-components has two warn nodes, per red-ac056-sh.log). Nothing in the bundle shows the emitted array is sorted, and TEST-024 is still 'Planned' and assigned to T-009 (traceability.md), so no test locks it.

AC-056 demands a companion multi-node fixture confirming the entry count scales 1:1 with node count plus exactly one summary entry, 'never fewer, never a second summary entry'. No such assertion is reachable from this bundle. The green and focused-tests logs show each dsl-warn-* fixture carrying only the same five generic assertions (exit / canonical diagnostic only / exact Resolver Evidence / schema agreement / no partial live artifact) -- no cardinality assertion by name. The report explicitly defers the primary mutation kills (a second summary entry; collapsing per-node entries into one) to T-005's TEST-056 suite, which is not in this bundle. The remaining lock is whole-document equality whose expected value is built by expected_warn_diagnostic(), described as 'mirroring _warn_diagnostic_detail byte-for-byte' -- a test-side reimplementation of the production formatter, which by construction cannot distinguish a wrong detail format from a correct one. From this bundle the tests cannot be shown to separate a correct implementation from a plausible wrong one.

Step 12's output-schema self-validation is this task's last defensive check before T-007 publishes (B3, a declared security boundary on a Security-Sensitive: true task), and the report states its hand-rolled draft-07 subset engine implements $ref, if/then/else, oneOf, propertyNames, pattern, uniqueItems and minItems. Both negative fixtures in the bundle defeat it with the same trivial shape, {"type":"object","required":["__t004_test_only_impossible_field__"]}, exercising only the 'required' keyword; the positive path runs against a deliberately loosened stand-in (resolve-project-context-projection/context-projection.schema.json defines projectedComponent with additionalProperties: true, disclosed as looser than Epic A4's real schema). An engine that silently ignored every keyword except 'required' would pass all 141 assertions. The engine itself is not in the bundle, so its keyword handling cannot be inspected either.

findings.note: Undisclosed spec drift in the warn entry's detail. The frozen spec defines the detail as naming that node's capability_id/component_id/(declaration_index, only for a conditional_facets[].when node). The implementation, per the report, additionally embeds node_path (a 0-based child-index tree path) and DSL attributes (operator/field/reason), and emits declaration_index as None for trigger nodes. The addition is defensible -- the spec's three-part key is not in fact unique for two warn leaves under one component's trigger tree, so the spec's own uniqueness clause cannot hold without it -- but the divergence is not recorded in the report's 'Specification Differences' section, and it changes the committed artifact's field content that AC-056's own assertion text describes.

Contradictory, untranscribed gate result. The implementation report records `check-workflow-state.sh --feature epic-193-a5-capability-resolver` as FAILED (exit 1, 'stage-provenance: task plan hash is stale') and carries it under Unresolved Items; the contract comment authored the same day asserts the same script 'returns workflow-state: ok exit 0 in both modes'. No command transcript for either run appears anywhere in the bundle's qg evidence, so neither statement is checkable.

For a tdd-required, Risk: high task, the AC-056 increment's own RED/GREEN pair (red-ac056-{sh,ps1}.log 138/3, green-ac056-{sh,ps1}.log 141/0) is referenced only in the contract's free-text comment, never in any check's red_evidence/green_evidence field. Those fields still pair the pre-AC-056 red-sh.log/red-ps1.log (107/14, captured against a code state that predates the fix) with a post-fix 141/0 green, so the contract's machine-readable TDD pair straddles two different implementations.

Report inaccuracy in the original RED account: it states 'the 14 failures are exactly this task's own 4 new fixtures' own assertions (5 + 4 + 5 + 5)' -- that sums to 19 -- and explains only one vacuous pass. The log actually shows 19 new assertions of which 14 failed and five passed vacuously (four 'no partial live artifact' plus one 'no Resolver Evidence written'). The RED itself is genuine; only the narrative miscounts.
